fields.description: The name of the claim that includes a list of user groups.
fields.label: Groups Claim

fields.description: Whether a login by someone without a Frappe user account creates one. "Use Social Login Key Setting" follows the Sign-ups field of the Social Login Key, falling back to the site's website signup setting, which is what Frappe's own social logins do. "Always Create Users" provisions everyone the identity provider lets through, which is only safe when the provider restricts who may reach this callback.
fields.label: User Provisioning
fields.options:
Use Social Login Key Setting
Always Create Users
Never Create Users

fields.description: The User Type given to users this app creates. Frappe overrides the two standard types on every save - a user holding any role with desk access becomes a System User, everyone else a Website User (User.set_system_user) - so on a site where System Users are billed seats, the role profiles you map decide the cost. A custom User Type is honoured as set.
fields.label: User Type For New Users

fields.description: Refuses a login when the identity provider says the email address has not been verified. Users are matched to Frappe accounts by email address, so an unverified one lets someone who registered another person's address take over their account. Providers that do not send the claim are unaffected.
fields.label: Require A Verified Email Address

fields.description: Deprecated, and hidden unless it is already on. Also matches a login to a Frappe user whose username equals the identity provider's user id claim, when nothing else matched. It exists only for users provisioned by versions of this app that stored the claim there; the claim is not a Frappe username, so it can match an unrelated account that happens to carry that name. Sites that have never run those versions should leave it off - turn it off and save, and it disappears.
fields.label: Match Users By Username (Deprecated)

fields.description: Verifies the signature of the id token against the signing keys of the identity provider. Turn this off only to debug a provider whose keys cannot be reached: an unverified id token is a bearer of unauthenticated claims, including the groups that decide the user's roles.
fields.label: Verify ID Token Signature

fields.description: The JWKS endpoint of the identity provider, for example https://auth.example.com/application/o/erpnext/jwks/. Leave empty to read it from the provider's OpenID discovery document.
fields.label: JWKS URL

fields.description: The expected "iss" claim of the id token. When set, tokens issued by a different issuer are rejected, and the discovery document is read from this URL. Defaults to the base URL of the Social Login Key.
fields.label: Issuer

fields.description: On by default, and what this app has always done: the groups in the token decide the user's role profiles, roles and module profile. Turn it off for a site that uses the identity provider to sign people in and to close their accounts when they leave, and assigns roles in the ERP by hand. Nothing below is then read or written - not the mappings, not the fallbacks, not "When No Group Matches", not "Disable Users With No Mapped Group" - and a login leaves the roles the ERP gave someone exactly as they are. Keeping directory groups in step with ERP roles costs more than it saves at some sizes; this is the switch for that.
fields.label: Manage Roles From The Identity Provider
Fallback Role Profiles
fields.description: If a user has no matching group mappings, they will be assigned these fallback role profiles. Consider leaving this empty: a fallback grants permissions to a user the identity provider said nothing about, and it counts as a mapped group, so with "Disable Users With No Mapped Group" on nobody is ever unmapped and that option can never fire.

fields.label: Group To Role Mappings
fields.description: Map OIDC groups to ERPNext roles. This assigns permissions allowing users to access data and make changes based on their role.

fields.label: Group To Role Grants
fields.description: Map OIDC groups to individual Roles. Where the profile mappings above compete - a role profile is a single Link on Frappe v15, so only the highest-priority match is assigned - these add up: a user in three mapped groups is granted all three roles, which is how "everything an accounts user has, and approval on top" is expressed. Only the roles named in this table are ever taken away, so a role granted here by hand in Frappe survives every login.

What to do when the identity provider returns no group that matches a mapping above and no fallback role profile is configured. "Keep Existing Roles" leaves the user's current roles untouched, "Remove All Roles" strips them so that removing a user from every group in the identity provider de-provisions them, and "Deny Login" refuses the login instead.
fields.label: When No Group Matches
fields.options:
Keep Existing Roles
Remove All Roles
Deny Login

fields.description: Disables the Frappe account of a user whose groups match no mapping above or below, and grant no fallback profile. Refusing the login is not the same as closing the account: a user denied at the door keeps an enabled account, and with it its API keys, its seat and its local password, none of which the identity provider can revoke. This composes with the setting above rather than replacing it - that one still decides what happens to the roles - so leaving it on "Keep Existing Roles" and turning this on lets group membership gate access without this app ever touching anybody's roles. A user whose group comes back is enabled again at their next login, so a membership removed by mistake is not permanent; by the same token, an account disabled by hand here is reopened if the provider still vouches for it. Administrator, Guest and the last enabled System Manager are never disabled, and never stripped of their roles either - an enabled account without the role that makes it useful is the same lockout. The guard is logged when it fires. Off by default.
fields.label: Disable Users With No Mapped Group

fields.description: If a user has no matching group mappings, they will be assigned this fallback module profile.
fields.label: Fallback Module Profile
Group To Module Mappings
fields.description: Map OIDC groups to ERPNext modules. This controls which modules are visible on the workspace/sidebar for the user.

fields.label: Enable Reconciliation
fields.description: Asks the identity provider on a schedule which users still exist, are still enabled and are still in which groups, and applies the answer. Nothing in OpenID Connect pushes this: removing someone from a group, or from the directory, otherwise reaches Frappe only at their next login - which, once they are gone, never comes.
How often a run is allowed, checked inside the task itself: the scheduler calls it every 15 minutes and it returns immediately unless this much time has passed since the last run.
fields.label: Frequency
When A User Is Gone Or Disabled
fields.description: What to do with a Frappe user the directory no longer has, or has disabled. "Report Only" writes to the log and changes nothing. The other two strip the role profiles and module profile first, so that a user re-enabled locally does not return with the entitlements they left with.
fields.options:
Report Only
Remove All Roles
Disable User

fields.description: Off by default, in which case only users who have signed in through this provider at least once are reconciled - a social login record is what ties a Frappe user to a directory entry. Turn it on to reconcile every enabled user instead, matching them to the directory by email address, so that an account somebody created here by hand is closed too when that person leaves. Read what that means first: a user the directory has never heard of - a service account, an integration, a contractor set up locally - is indistinguishable from somebody who has left, and will be disabled. List those below.
fields.label: Reconcile Every Enabled User

fields.description: Users this reconciliation must never act on.
fields.label: Never Reconcile These Users
Directory URL
fields.description: For Keycloak, the realm URL - the same base URL the Social Login Key uses, for example https://idp.example.com/realms/erp. For authentik, its base URL.

fields.label: Service Account Client ID
fields.description: A Keycloak client with client authentication and service account roles on, whose service account holds view-users from realm-management.

fields.label: API Token
fields.description: authentik matches users by email address: what it puts in `sub` depends on the provider's subject mode.

Shared secret for the webhook endpoint at /api/method/oidc_extended.reconciliation.webhook/<provider>. Keycloak has no webhook of its own; an event listener provider deployed into it can call this whenever a user or a group membership changes, and the user is then re-checked against the directory at once instead of waiting for the next scheduled run. The call must present the secret as a bearer token or sign the body with it (HMAC-SHA256). Without a secret the endpoint is closed.
fields.label: Webhook Secret
